short-jobs-around-the-house.title: Pulling Loose Hair from a Hairbrush
short-jobs-around-the-house.description: After brushing, a few loose strands are caught between the bristles. A small comb helps lift them out.
short-jobs-around-the-house.solvingTip: Start with the tool with a row of teeth. Then think about the thin things it lifts out of the brush.

words.HAIRBRUSH: Tool with rows of bristles used to smooth hair
words.BRISTLE: One short, firm fiber sticking out of a brush
words.STRAND: One long, thin piece of hair
words.COMB: Flat tool with a row of teeth for untangling hair
words.TEETH: The points in a row along a comb
words.HANDLE: Part of a brush you hold in your hand
words.LIFT: Raise the loose hair out of the brush
words.SNAG: Get caught on a bristle as you pull
words.ROW: Line of bristles with one beside another
words.TRASH: Waste that goes into the bin

notes.HAIRBRUSH: A hairbrush has several rows of bristles. A comb usually has a single row of teeth.
notes.BRISTLE: A bristle may bend as it passes through hair. Loose hairs can catch between the bristles.
notes.STRAND: A strand is one hair. Several strands can collect in a small bundle at the base of a brush.

getting-out-the-door-4.title: Folding a Handkerchief for a Coat Pocket
getting-out-the-door-4.description: A clean square of cloth folds small enough to slip into a coat before a walk.
getting-out-the-door-4.solvingTip: Think of getting a coat ready. Try the clue for the little pouch sewn into it, then the words about making a square of cloth smaller.

words.COTTON: Soft fiber often used to make handkerchiefs
words.FOLD: Bend a cloth so one part lies over another
words.POCKET: Small pouch sewn into a coat
words.CLEAN: Freshly washed and free of dirt
words.CREASE: Line left where the cloth is folded
words.SQUARE: Shape with four equal sides and four right angles
words.TUCK: Slip an item neatly into a small space
words.COAT: Outer garment worn when going out in cool weather
words.CLOTH: Fabric used to make a handkerchief
words.CORNER: Point where two sides of the cloth meet
words.FIT: Be the right size for the pocket
words.FLAT: Smooth with no raised folds or lumps
words.HEM: Sewn edge that keeps the cloth from fraying

notes.COTTON: Cotton handkerchiefs are washable and absorb moisture.
notes.FOLD: Bringing one half over the other makes the cloth smaller without cutting it.
notes.POCKET: A folded handkerchief lies flatter inside a coat and is easy to pull out.

garden-birds-and-insects-4.title: A Paper Wasp Scraping Wood from a Fence
garden-birds-and-insects-4.description: A wasp works at a weathered fence, gathering tiny wood fibers that will become nest material.
garden-birds-and-insects-4.solvingTip: Begin with the clue for the barrier around the yard. Then try the clues about what the insect does with the little bits it collects.

words.WASP: Flying insect that chews wood to make a papery nest
words.SCRAPE: Rub away a little material from the surface of a board
words.PAPER: Thin material that the wasp's dried nest resembles
words.WOOD: Hard material from a tree that can be cut into boards
words.FENCE: Barrier made of boards around a yard
words.CHEW: Work something between the jaws to break it up
words.FIBER: One thin strand in a piece of wood
words.NEST: Place the insect builds to raise its young
words.GRAY: Color of some weathered fence boards
words.BOARD: Flat piece of wood used to build a fence
words.WING: Body part the insect uses to fly
words.DRY: Lose moisture as the nest material hardens
words.MIX: Combine wood fibers with moisture from the mouth
words.GATHER: Collect small bits from several spots

notes.WASP: Paper wasps gather fibers from weathered wood and chew them into a soft mixture.
notes.SCRAPE: A wasp can work its jaws against the surface to loosen a tiny bit of wood.
notes.PAPER: The chewed fibers dry into thin layers that look and feel like paper.
